Twenty Third Indian Antarctic Expedition
Ministry o f Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 21, pp 279-303
Environmental Management Services at  
Maitri, Antarctica
G Veerabhadraiah and Anil Jain
Environment Division, Engineers India Ltd., New Delhi
Engineers India Limited (EIL) started its association with the Indian 
Antarctic Program by participating in the summer part of the 23rd Indian 
Antarctic Expedition (XXIII-IAE). EIL provided its services in reviewing 
Wastewater Management at Maitri, the permanent Indian Research Station 
in Antarctica. The work carried out by Environment Division of EIL for the 
study Wastewater Management at Maitri is covered here.
In order to carry out the study, a 10 point methodology has been adopted 
covering various aspects such as collecting front-end information, review 
of design data, obtaining operating and site specific information and their 
analysis to arrive at final conclusions and recommendations. Site work was 
initiated with collection of all available data/information with respect to 
existing wastewater management facilities. In order to get the design, 
operating and maintenance details of existing biodiscs treating the effluent 
from Maitri, EIL communicated with system suppliers i.e. Klargester 
Environmental Engineering, UK. A database has been created with all the 
information obtained and the same was made available to Expedition Leader. 
Also collected relevant data on wastewater generation and its handling 
associated with summer camp facilities. Historical operating data available 
from earlier expeditions has been compiled. Also collected site-specific 
data as well as feedback from leaders of past expeditions and inmates 
(wintering personnel) of Maitri to obtain the first hand information. At the 
end of the expedition, various interim measures have been suggested for up 
keeping of the wastewater management facilities pending the execution of 
modifications required, and the same were discussed and explained to 
Expedition Leader and Logistic Team.
After the expedition, the existing system has been reviewed with all 
the available information collected at site and the fresh data collected from 
NCAOR. Conclusions have been made highlighting various limitations of

the existing facilities along with the recommendation to overcome the same 
suggesting the action plan. While submitting the report, a presentation has 
also been made to the Technical Committee in this regard. Subsequently 
EIL has submitted proposal to implement the modifications required 
suggesting the methodology of execution in phased manner.
Engineers India Limited (EIL) having its headquarters in New Delhi 
and offices in India and abroad, is a premier consulting organization in 
South-east Asia which provides value-added services in varied fields of 
engineering using state-of-the-art technology. EIL is looking forward to 
actively contribute towards this mission of great importance to mankind 
and to the nation by offering its services for any engineering and 
technological requirements.
INTRODUCTION
Maitri - India's permanent Antarctic station was built in 1989 and is 
located in Schirmacher Oasis region in Princes Maud Land in East 
Antarctica. It serves for year round scientific exploration and research studies 
by various organizations. Every year, Indian expedition is conducted with 
scientists, engineers, and logistic personnel with half the team stay for only 
austral summer and the rest for the entire year. Maitri wais designed for 
about 25 personnel with basic infrastructure and life support systems. 
Summer team stays in specially designed timber huts.
M/s National Centre for Antarctic & Ocean Research (NCAOR), Goa, 
under Department of Development (DOD), Government of India, is the 
nodal organization for the co-ordination and implementation of the Indian 
Antarctic Program including the up-keep of India's permanent (year round) 
station - Maitri at Antarctica. In 2003, M/s NCAOR invited Engineers India 
Limited (EIL), New Delhi to participate in Indian Antarctic Expedition to 
carryout structural assessment of Maitri and review of its wastewater 
management system. This report is about the work carried out by 
Environment Division of EIL for the review of wastewater management 
system.
FIELDS OF INVESTIGATION
The existing wastewater treatment units and associated facilities 
required detailed study for review and their improvement to meet the 
applicable effluent discharge standards inline with Madrid Protocol
